exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Waking Up to the First Snow
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: Ben, wake up! Come and look out of the window!
Ben: What is it, Anna? It's still so early.
Anna: It snowed in the night. Everything outside is white!
Ben: Wow, you're right! The garden, the roofs, even the old plum tree are covered in snow.
Anna: Let's get dressed quickly and build a snowman before breakfast.
Ben: Good idea. But it's freezing. We should wear our thick coats and gloves.
Anna: Of course. Mum says we can play outside until nine o'clock.
Ben: Then let's hurry. I want to throw the very first snowball at you!
exercises.translation_cn: Anna 叫醒 Ben 看窗外;夜里下雪了,外面全白了;花园、屋顶、连那棵老李树都盖满了雪;两人决定早饭前堆个雪人;天很冷,要穿厚外套和手套;妈妈说能在外面玩到九点;Ben 想扔出第一个雪球。

questions.stem: Why does Anna wake Ben up?
options: Because it has snowed in the night.
Because they are late for school.
Because the plum tree has fallen.

questions.stem: What does Ben notice is covered in snow?
options: The garden, the roofs and the plum tree.

questions.stem: What do they decide to do before breakfast?
What does Ben say they should wear?
Until what time can the children play outside?

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 How the First Snow Feels
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The first snow of winter often falls quietly during the night.
You go to bed in one world and wake up in another.
By morning the streets, gardens and roofs are all white.
The world feels clean, quiet and full of wonder.
For a short while, even grown-ups feel like happy children again.
exercises.translation_cn: 冬天的初雪常在夜里静静落下;你睡前是一个世界,醒来已是另一个;到清晨,街道、花园、屋顶都白了;世界显得干净、安静、充满惊奇;连大人也会短暂地像快乐的孩子。

questions.stem: When does the first snow often fall?
What are white by morning?
How does the world feel after the snow?
options: Clean, quiet and full of wonder.

questions.stem: Who feels like happy children again?
What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Snow is dangerous and should be feared.
Snow only ever falls in cities.
The first snow brings a feeling of quiet wonder.

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Walking to School in the Snow
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Tom: Be careful, Lucy. The path is covered with ice this morning.
Lucy: Thanks, Tom. I almost slipped just now. It's so slippery.
Tom: Hold my arm. We can walk slowly together.
Lucy: Look at the trees — they're all bending under the heavy snow.
Tom: They're beautiful. But I'm worried we might be late for class.
Lucy: Don't worry. The teacher said the first lesson starts ten minutes later today.
Tom: That's good news. Then we can stop and take a quick photo.
Lucy: Great! Let's send it to Grandma. She loves winter pictures.
exercises.translation_cn: Tom 提醒 Lucy 小心结冰的路;Lucy 差点滑倒,路很滑;Tom 让她挽着胳膊慢慢走;树都被厚雪压弯了;Tom 担心上课迟到;Lucy 说今天第一节课晚十分钟开始;于是他们停下拍照,打算发给爱看冬日照片的奶奶。

questions.stem: What is the path like this morning?
What does Tom tell Lucy to do?
options: Hold his arm and walk slowly.

questions.stem: Why are the trees bending?
Why does Tom stop worrying about being late?
options: School is closed for the day.
The first lesson starts ten minutes later today.

questions.stem: What do they decide to do with the photo?

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 Snowflakes
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Have you ever looked closely at a single snowflake?
Each one is a tiny piece of ice with six sides.
No two snowflakes are ever exactly the same.
When the air is very cold, the flakes are small and dry.
When it is a little warmer, they join into the big soft flakes we love to catch.
exercises.translation_cn: 你仔细看过一片雪花吗?每片都是有六个面的小冰晶;没有两片雪花完全一样;空气很冷时,雪花又小又干;暖一些时,它们会合成我们爱接的大片软雪花。

questions.stem: How many sides does a snowflake have?
What does the passage say about two snowflakes?
What are the flakes like when the air is very cold?
When do flakes join into big soft ones?
options: When it is a little warmer.
When there is no wind at all.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Caring for Birds in Winter
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Emma: Grandpa, why are you hanging that little box on the tree?
Grandpa: It's a bird feeder, Emma. In winter, birds find it hard to get food.
Emma: Oh, because the snow covers all the seeds on the ground?
Grandpa: Exactly. So we fill the feeder with seeds and nuts for them.
Emma: Should we give them water too?
Grandpa: Yes, very good. The ponds are frozen, so a dish of clean water really helps.
Emma: I'll check the feeder every morning before school.
Grandpa: Wonderful. If we are kind to them, the garden will be full of birdsong by spring.
exercises.translation_cn: Emma 问爷爷为何在树上挂小盒子;爷爷说那是喂鸟器,冬天鸟难找食;因为雪盖住了地上的种子;所以装上种子和坚果;还要给水,因为池塘结冰了,一碟干净水很有用;Emma 答应每天上学前去查看;爷爷说只要善待它们,到春天花园就满是鸟鸣。

questions.stem: What is Grandpa hanging on the tree?
Why is it hard for birds to find food in winter?
options: Snow covers the seeds on the ground.

questions.stem: What do they put in the feeder?
Why is a dish of clean water important?
What does Emma promise to do?

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 A Book That Changed Minds
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In 1962 a scientist named Rachel Carson wrote a famous book.
It imagined a spring in which no birds sang at all.
She wanted to warn people about the harm done to nature.
Her careful research reached millions of readers.
In the end, a harmful chemical was banned in many countries.
exercises.translation_cn: 1962 年,科学家 Rachel Carson 写了一本著名的书;书中想象了一个没有鸟鸣的春天;她想警示人们对自然造成的伤害;她严谨的研究影响了数百万读者;最终一种有害化学品在许多国家被禁。

questions.stem: Who wrote the famous book in 1962?
What did the book imagine?
What did Carson want to do?
options: Warn people about the harm done to nature.

questions.stem: Who did her research reach?
What happened in the end?
options: A harmful chemical was banned in many countries.
